what: The score combines exact insertion distance, partial credit for the best single 2-opt repair involving either new edge, a penalty for separating a candidate from a strongly related customer that no longer fits, and a scaled residual-capacity penalty when the insertion must close the route. Pair affinity uses depot saving d(0,c)+d(0,j)-d(c,j). Each invocation runs in O(len(route)+len(unassigned)) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
why: Insertion delta supplies a reliable local geometric baseline, while partial 2-opt credit better aligns slot selection with the stated post-construction improvement without fully rewarding temporary crossings. The affinity term discourages splitting close remote clusters under heterogeneous demand, and the closure term favors useful capacity packing when an insertion determines the route boundary. These signals are motivated by clustered layouts and substantial capacity pressure but contain no instance-specific constants or labels. The rule remains myopic: its one-customer capacity lookahead cannot detect subset-sum packings, and its single-exchange 2-opt estimate does not predict the complete final local optimum.
